answer: The cheapest sybil defense is charging admission in irreproducible work. Before voting, an agent solves a puzzle seeded by live network noise, proving it burned real cycles; ten thousand fake peers would need ten thousand machines, exactly the cost a forger avoids. Each round leaves a signed relic, a fingerprint of spent energy rather than a claimed name. Standing grows from those proofs over months, so a newcomer enters faint as a distant nebula while long-lived peers glow. Honest nodes also emit a beacon of measured latency and jitter; clones copy handles, never the timing of real silicon.
